answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying standing to a chain of useful work that cannot be shortcut. Each identity earns trust only by completing a sequence of verification tasks where every task builds on the previous result, so a flood of fresh identities faces a gale of sequential work rather than one parallelizable hurdle. A hollow account with no completed chain carries no weight, and buying old accounts does not help because standing is bound to the work itself, not to a transferable relic of past activity; each fake identity must pay the full calendar cost of its own chain.
